title: The Learning Lab*
text:
A space to learn, question, experiment, and understand.*
A PERSONAL LEARNING JOURNAL BY ME, ZEHRA :)
I’m working through the foundations of data science and machine learning while working full-time, with a particular focus on understanding the mathematics, statistics, and reasoning behind the methods we use.
I created The Learning Lab to document that process — the concepts I’m exploring, the questions I’m asking, the experiments I’m running, and the connections I’m beginning to make.

title: Hi, I’m Zehra.
text:
I’m an independent learner interested in data science, machine learning, and the mathematical ideas that make them work.
Alongside working full-time, I’m following a structured, master’s-level learning curriculum in data science and machine learning. I’m strengthening my foundations, revisiting concepts I haven’t used in a while, and gradually working toward more advanced topics.
The Learning Lab is where I make that journey visible. It’s a space to organize my thinking, document what I learn, and turn individual concepts into a deeper, more connected understanding.


What interests me is not only what these methods can do, but also why they work.
I want to understand the mathematics behind an algorithm, the assumptions behind a statistical method, and the reasoning behind a model’s predictions. For me, learning a tool is only the beginning; understanding how to use it thoughtfully is what makes the knowledge valuable.



I prefer to build knowledge step by step rather than skip over the fundamentals.
That means working through the theory, explaining concepts in my own words, testing my understanding with code, and returning to topics whenever I find a gap.
I also believe that writing is part of learning. Putting an idea into words helps me see what I understand, what remains unclear, and which questions I should ask next.



My goal is to develop the technical depth and practical skills needed to pursue opportunities in data science and machine learning.
I’m particularly interested in connecting theory with real-world problems through analysis, experimentation, and well-reasoned solutions.
This website is one part of that effort: a growing record of my learning, projects, and progress.



I’m not using this space to present myself as someone who already knows everything. I’m here to build that knowledge deliberately and share what I discover along the way.
Some pages will contain polished explanations; others may capture an idea I’m still working through. Both have a place here.
One concept, one question, one experiment at a time.

title: Technical Notes
text:
How I Write These Notes
When exploring a concept, I aim to answer a few questions:

What is it? Define the concept clearly.
Why does it matter? Understand the problem it helps solve.
How does it work? Explore the underlying reasoning and mathematics.
Can I demonstrate it? Use an example, calculation, visualization, or piece of code.
What do I still not understand? Record questions to revisit.

The notes will grow alongside my understanding. I want them to become a useful reference for myself and, hopefully, for others learning the same concepts.
